turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Hello, please have a seat. I'm Dr. Chen. I know waiting for results is stressful, so I will explain the findings clearly and we can go step by step.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.expected_user_text: Thank you, doctor. I have been very anxious. I keep having pain after meals, and I am worried this could be something serious.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: I understand why you feel worried. Your tests do not suggest cancer, which is reassuring. They show gallstones with gallbladder inflammation, and this can explain your pain and tiredness.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.expected_user_text: That is a relief, but surgery still scares me. I have never had general anesthesia, and I am worried about complications.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Those concerns are completely reasonable. For this planned laparoscopic surgery, serious complications are uncommon. Before the operation, anesthesia will review your health, and during surgery your breathing, oxygen, blood pressure, and heart rhythm are monitored continuously.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.expected_user_text: That helps. What would recovery look like, and how much time should I plan away from work and family responsibilities?

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Most patients stay one night or sometimes go home the same day. Pain is usually strongest in the first few days and improves with medication. Many people return to light daily activities within one to two weeks.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.expected_user_text: Could I wait until work is less busy, or would postponing it make things worse?

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: It is not an emergency today, so we can plan around your schedule. I would avoid delaying for months, because repeated attacks can cause stronger pain, infection, or a more urgent operation later.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.expected_user_text: I see. What should I watch for at home before surgery, and what should I prepare if I decide to proceed?

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Call us urgently for fever, worsening pain, yellow eyes, or persistent vomiting. If you choose surgery, we will give you a checklist for medicines, fasting, transport, and home support. You can also take a few days to discuss this with your family.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.expected_user_text: Thank you. I still feel nervous, but I understand the situation better and can make a decision more calmly.
